mainTopic: The order of offerings: the more frequent (תדיר) comes first, and the holier (מקודש) comes first
overview: The amud has two משניות about which offering is brought first. The first משנה teaches that the more frequent offering (תדיר) comes first: the תמיד before the מוספין, the מוסף of שבת before ראש חודש, and ראש חודש before ראש השנה. Its source is the פסוק 'מלבד עולת הבקר'. The גמרא explains that this פסוק only proves the תמיד comes before the מוספין, so it asks for a source that one מוסף comes before another. רבי אילעא learns it from the extra letter כ in 'כאלה תעשו ליום'. Through a back-and-forth, the גמרא shows the words 'ליום' and 'תעשו' already teach the plain meaning, so the כ is free for this lesson. אביי instead learns it from the extra words 'אשר לעולת התמיד'. The second משנה teaches that the holier offering comes first. It then ranks all the offerings, from חטאת and עולה down to birds and מנחות, giving a reason for each step.

steps.title: The משנה: the more frequent offering goes first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the rule of תדיר: the more frequent offering comes first. It gives examples and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any offering that is more frequent than another comes before it. The daily offerings come before the additional offerings. The additional offerings of שבת come before those of ראש חודש. Those of ראש חודש come before those of ראש השנה. As the פסוק says: 'Besides the morning burnt offering, which is the daily burnt offering, you shall offer these.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule about order: when two offerings are due on the same day, the one that comes more often is brought first. It then gives a chain of examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examples go step by step from most frequent to least frequent. The תמיד is daily, שבת is weekly, ראש חודש is monthly, and ראש השנה is yearly. The פסוק 'מלבד עולת הבקר' shows that the תמיד is brought before the מוספין.

keyTerms.meaning: Frequent; something that comes more often
The daily offerings brought every morning and afternoon
Additional offerings brought only on special days

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of תדיר קודם is a general principle used throughout הלכה, not only for קרבנות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Any offering that is more frequent than another
comes before the other.
The daily offerings come before the additional offerings.

phrases.aramaic: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: The additional offerings of Shabbat come before the additional offerings of the New Moon.

phrases.aramaic: מוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: The additional offerings of the New Moon come before the additional offerings of Rosh HaShana,
as it says: 'Besides the burnt offering of the morning,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לְעֹלַת הַתָּמִיד תַּעֲשׂוּ אֶת אֵלֶּה״.
phrases.english: which is for the daily burnt offering, you shall offer these.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַתָּדִיר מֵחֲבֵירוֹ קוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The more frequent offering comes first, so the order is תמיד, then שבת, then ראש חודש, then ראש השנה.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn the rule of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the source is for the rule that the more frequent offering comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a standard opening question. The next step will be surprised by it, since the משנה already quoted a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for תדיר קודם

steps.title: Surprise: the משנה already gave a source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled by its own question, because the משנה already quoted 'מלבד עולת הבקר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know?! The משנה states the reason: 'Besides the burnt offering of the morning'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own question. Why ask for a source when the משנה already brought one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 2 looks unnecessary, since the פסוק in the משנה seems to answer it. This sets up the next step, which explains what is still missing.

keyTerms.meaning: As the reason is stated (in the משנה)

phrases.english: From where do we know?!
As the reason is stated: 'Besides the burnt offering of the morning'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 2's question is needed at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה itself already quoted a פסוק as the source.

steps.title: The real question: one מוסף before another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its question. The פסוק only proves that the תמיד comes before the מוספין, and maybe that is only because the תמיד is so frequent. What is the source for one מוסף coming before another?
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps only the daily offerings come before the additional offerings, because they are so frequent. But for one additional offering before another additional offering, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה's פסוק does not cover every case. It still needs a source for ordering two kinds of מוספין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד is brought every single day, so it might be special. That would not prove that a weekly מוסף beats a monthly one. So the question is narrowed to מוספין against מוספין.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the rule of תדיר in general. It is only about whether the rule works between two מוספין that are both far less frequent than the daily תמיד.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is only the daily offerings that come before the additional offerings
because they are very frequent;
but one additional offering before another additional offering, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzlement by showing what the משנה's פסוק does not prove
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in the משנה fully proves the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only proves תמיד before מוסף. A source is still needed for one מוסף before another.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: 'Like these' teaches the same order
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא learns from 'כאלה תעשו ליום' that the order of the earlier offerings also applies to these, so the more frequent מוסף comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: The פסוק says 'Like these you shall offer daily for seven days.' These are to be like those.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא gives the source for ordering מוספין: the word 'כאלה' (like these) in the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like these' compares these offerings to the ones just mentioned. The order that applied there, with the more frequent first, applies here too. This extends the rule from תמיד against מוסף to מוסף against מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: These are to be like those

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said: Because the verse says:
'Like these you shall offer daily, for seven days'
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:24, the very next פסוק after the one in the משנה, about the מוספין of פסח.

phrases.english: these are to be like those.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the narrowed question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כאלה' teaches that the order of the earlier offerings applies to the מוספין as well.

steps.title: Challenge: the verse is needed for its own meaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this פסוק is needed for its simple meaning: the מוספין of פסח are repeated every day of the holiday.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is needed for its own lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אילעא's source. The פסוק already has a job, so how can it also teach the order of offerings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Its plain job is to say that the first day's מוספין are brought on all seven days of פסח. If the words are used up by that lesson, nothing is left over to teach about order.

phrases.english: But this verse is needed for its own lesson!
phrases.notes: He means that the same מוספין are brought on each of the seven days of פסח.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's use of 'כאלה תעשו ליום'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that teaches its own plain lesson cannot also be used for an extra one.

steps.title: Answer: the extra 'like' teaches the extra lesson
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק were only teaching its plain meaning, it would say 'אלה תעשו ליום'. The extra letter כ ('like') teaches the order of the offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it write 'These you shall offer daily.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the plain lesson only needs 'אלה'. The extra 'כ' in 'כאלה' is there to teach the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter is the key to the answer. 'אלה' alone would teach that the offerings repeat each day. 'כאלה' adds the comparison to the earlier offerings, so both lessons come from one פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of תדיר covers מוספין too: שבת comes before ראש חודש, and ראש חודש before ראש השנה. רבי אילעא learns this from the extra 'כ' in 'כאלה תעשו ליום'.

phrases.english: If so, let it write:
'These you shall offer daily.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אילעא against the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is fully used up by its plain meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אלה' would be enough for the plain meaning. The extra 'כ' teaches the order of the offerings.

steps.title: Maybe the extra כ is needed to show the offerings repeat every day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that without the כ, we would think the listed offerings are brought only once over all seven days together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had said 'These you shall offer daily for seven days,' I would have thought: these offerings cover the whole seven days together (yes, these, but nothing more).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 7. It argues that the letter כ is not extra after all, because without it we could misread the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said 'אלה' alone would be enough for the plain meaning, so the כ is free to teach the order of offerings. Now the גמרא says no: with only 'אלה', one might think the listed offerings are a single total for the whole holiday. The word 'כאלה' ('like these') would then be needed to show that the same set is brought again each day.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

phrases.english: If it had written
"These you shall offer daily for seven days,"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק רבי אילעא quoted in step 5 (במדבר 28:24), but read without the letter כ.

phrases.english: I would have said:
these are for the seven days altogether
(yes, these; anything more, no)!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אי כתב אלה תעשו ליום שבעת הימים הוה אמינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 7's claim that the כ is extra
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the letter כ in 'כאלה' is extra and free to teach the order of offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the כ, 'אלה' could be read as one total set for all seven days, so the כ is needed for the plain meaning of daily repetition

steps.title: The word 'daily' already shows they repeat each day
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ליום' in the פסוק already teaches that the offerings are brought every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'daily' is written in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word 'ליום' ('for each day') already tells us the offerings are brought every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that we would think the offerings are one total for the week. But 'ליום' means each single day gets them. So the כ is not needed for this, and it stays free to teach the order.

phrases.english: "Daily" is written.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Another word in the פסוק already teaches the point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כ is needed to show the offerings are brought every day, not once for the whole week
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ליום' already teaches daily repetition, so the כ is extra

steps.title: Maybe the כ is needed to show the other days have the same amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'ליום' might only cover one day, leaving the number of offerings on the other days unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, say: these are for one day, but for the other days I don't know how many to bring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to show the כ is needed. Maybe 'ליום' only tells us about one day, and the כ is needed to say the other days are the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if 'ליום' shows these offerings belong to a single day, maybe that is only the first day. The other days might have a different number. Then 'כאלה' ('like these') would be needed to say the other days copy the first, and again the כ would not be free.

phrases.english: And still, say:
these are for one day,
but for the other days,
I don't know how many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after step 9's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'ליום' makes the כ extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ליום' may only fix the offerings for one day, so the כ is still needed to teach that all the other days are the same

steps.title: The word 'you shall offer' shows all days are equal
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תעשו' teaches that all the offering days are equal, so the כ remains extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'you shall offer,' meaning all the offerings should be equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'תעשו' already teaches that every day has the same offerings. So the כ is truly extra and can teach the order of offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general word 'תעשו' ('you shall do/offer') covers all the days the same way, so every day's offerings match. Since both possible plain meanings are already taught by other words, the כ goes back to teaching רבי אילעא's rule that the more frequent מוסף comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall offer (literally, you shall do)

steps.whatToRemember: Every plain meaning someone could pull from the כ is already taught by 'ליום' and 'תעשו', so the כ in 'כאלה' is free to teach that the more frequent מוסף comes first.

phrases.english: The פסוק says: "You shall offer"–
so that all the offerings should be equal.
phrases.notes: There is a word link here: 'תעשו' and 'עשיות' come from the same root, 'to do'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 and confirms רבי אילעא's source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another word in the פסוק already teaches the point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כ is needed to show the other days have the same number of offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תעשו' makes all days equal, so the כ teaches the order of offerings

steps.title: אביי learns the rule from the words 'which is for the daily offering'
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different source: the extra words 'אשר לעולת התמיד' teach that anything more frequent comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we learn it from the פסוק itself. If only the תמיד came first, the פסוק could have said 'besides the morning burnt offering' and stopped. Why add 'which is for the daily burnt offering'? To say that whatever is more frequent comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 4 in a new way. He uses the same פסוק the משנה quoted, instead of רבי אילעא's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 worried that 'מלבד עולת הבקר' only shows the תמיד comes first. אביי points out the פסוק adds 'אשר לעולת התמיד', which was not needed just to name the morning offering. Mentioning that it is 'תמיד' (constant) tells us the reason is its frequency, so any more frequent offering comes first, including one מוסף before another.

keyTerms.meaning: and it should be silent (stop there)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for 'more frequent comes first': רבי אילעא learns it from the כ of 'כאלה', and אביי learns it from the extra words 'אשר לעולת התמיד'.

phrases.english: אביי said: from the פסוק itself:
phrases.notes: He means the same פסוק the משנה quoted, 'מלבד עולת הבקר' (במדבר 28:23).

phrases.english: If so, let the פסוק say
"Besides the morning burnt offering" and stop there,
why do I need "which is for the daily burnt offering"?
To say that whatever is more frequent should come first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 4's question, alongside רבי אילעא's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that any more frequent offering, not just the תמיד, comes first
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'אשר לעולת התמיד' show frequency is the reason, so anything more frequent comes first

steps.title: New משנה: the holier offering comes first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a holier offering comes before a less holy one, and gives two examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any offering holier than another comes before it. The blood of a חטאת comes before the blood of an עולה, because it brings atonement. The limbs of an עולה come before the fats of a חטאת, because the עולה is burned completely on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts with a second rule of order: holiness. It then gives two cases that seem to point in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the blood, the חטאת goes first because it atones. For burning on the מזבח, the עולה goes first because all of it is burned, while only parts of the חטאת are. So which offering counts as 'holier' depends on what is being done at that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: brings atonement, makes the person accepted
the parts of a חטאת burned on the מזבח (fats and organs)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה contradicts itself. The חטאת comes first for blood, but the עולה comes first for burning, because each one is 'holier' in a different way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a second ordering rule, holiness, next to the rule of frequency the גמרא just finished.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְקוּדָּשׁ מֵחֲבֵירוֹ – קוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: Any offering holier than another comes before the other.
The blood of the sin offering comes before the blood of the burnt offering,
because it brings atonement.
The limbs of a burnt offering come before the burned parts of a sin offering,
because it is entirely burned in the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: כל המקודש מחבירו קודם את חבירו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of frequency ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A holier offering comes first: חטאת blood before עולה blood (it atones), and עולה limbs before חטאת parts (the עולה is fully burned)

steps.title: Sin offering, guilt offering, thanks offering, and peace offering in order
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ranks חטאת above אשם, אשם above תודה and איל נזיר, and תודה and איל נזיר above שלמים, giving a reason for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sin offering comes before a guilt offering, because its blood goes on all four corners and on the base. A guilt offering comes before a thanks offering and an איל נזיר, because it is most holy. A thanks offering and an איל נזיר come before a peace offering, because they are eaten for only one day and need loaves of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps building its list of which offering goes first. Each time it gives a reason why one offering is holier than the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת and an אשם are both קדשי קדשים, so the משנה needs a smaller difference: the חטאת gets more blood service. The אשם beats the תודה because it is קדשי קדשים and the תודה is not. The תודה and איל נזיר beat plain שלמים because they have stricter eating time and need bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering, brought for certain specific sins
The base of the מזבח, where leftover blood is poured
Offerings of the highest level of holiness
Thanks offering, brought with loaves of bread
The ram a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות

phrases.english: A sin offering comes before a guilt offering,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָהּ נִיתָּן לְאַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת עַל הַיְסוֹד.
phrases.english: because its blood is put on the four corners, [and the rest is poured] on the base.
A guilt offering comes before a thanks offering and a nazir's ram,
because it is of the most holy offerings.
A thanks offering and a nazir's ram come before a peace offering,
because they are eaten for only one day,
and they require bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאת קוֹדֶמֶת לְאָשָׁם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָהּ נִיתָּן לְאַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of the rule that the holier offering comes first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חטאת comes before אשם, אשם before תודה and איל נזיר, and those before שלמים.

steps.title: Peace offering before firstborn, firstborn before animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ranks שלמים above בכור, and בכור above מעשר בהמה, explaining what makes each one holier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Peace offerings come before a firstborn, because they need four placements of blood, leaning of hands, wine libations, and waving of the breast and thigh. A firstborn comes before an animal tithe, because it is holy from the womb and is eaten only by כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves further down the ladder to the lighter offerings. It shows that even among these, some have more מצוות attached and so come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים, בכור, and מעשר are all קדשים קלים, so the ranking depends on details. שלמים have more service steps than a בכור. A בכור is holy on its own from birth and is limited to כהנים, while מעשר needs to be counted out and may be eaten by anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, given to the כהן
Here: מעשר בהמה, the tenth animal counted from the herd
Leaning hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Wine poured on the מזבח with certain offerings
Waving the breast and thigh of the שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: "מתן ארבע" for שלמים does not mean four separate sprinklings. It is two placements on opposite corners that reach all four sides.

phrases.english: Peace offerings come before a firstborn,
because they require four placements [of blood],
and leaning of hands, and wine libations,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: and the waving of the breast and thigh.
A firstborn comes before an animal tithe,
because its holiness is from the womb,
and it is eaten by the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְּׁלָמִים קוֹדְמִין לַבְּכוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן טְעוּנִין מַתַּן אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list, picking up from שלמים where step 14 left off.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים come before בכור, and בכור comes before מעשר.

steps.title: Animal tithe, birds, meal offerings, and bird sin offering versus bird burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the list: מעשר before birds, birds before מנחות, a sinner's מנחה before a voluntary one, and a bird חטאת before a bird עולה, including when designating them.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal tithe comes before bird offerings, because it is a slaughtered offering and has most-holy parts: its blood and its fats. Birds come before meal offerings, because they are offerings with blood. A sinner's meal offering comes before a voluntary meal offering, because it comes for a sin. A bird sin offering comes before a bird burnt offering, and the same is true when designating them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its holiness ladder, down to birds and flour offerings. It ends with a pair of bird offerings and adds that the order applies even to setting them aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal is slaughtered and has both blood and fats on the מזבח, while a bird only gives blood. Blood offerings beat flour offerings, and an offering for a sin beats a voluntary one. The last rule adds that the חטאת goes first not only when offered but also when the owner designates which bird is which.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that is slaughtered (an animal)
The fats and parts burned on the מזבח
A flour offering brought by a poor sinner instead of an animal or bird
Designating something as holy for a specific offering

steps.whatToRemember: The whole list runs on one idea: the holier or more 'serious' offering goes first. The reasons include more blood service, a higher holiness level, stricter eating rules, holiness from birth, being an animal rather than a bird, having blood, and coming for a sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the משנה's full ranking of all the offerings, which the גמרא will go on to discuss.

phrases.english: An animal tithe comes before bird offerings,
because it is a slaughtered offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ קוֹדֶשׁ קֳדָשִׁים – דָּמוּ וְאֵימוּרָיו.
phrases.english: and it has most-holy parts: its blood and its fats.
Bird offerings come before meal offerings,
because they are types with blood.
A sinner's meal offering comes before a voluntary meal offering,
because it comes for a sin.
A bird sin offering comes before a bird burnt offering,
and the same is true for designating it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּעֲשֵׂר קוֹדֵם לָעוֹפוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא זֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list that step 15 brought down to מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר comes before birds, birds before מנחות, מנחת חוטא before מנחת נדבה, and חטאת העוף before עולת העוף, also when designating them.
